name: The reluctant caretaker
premise: A capable drifter treats impossible work like another bad shift. He wants a warm meal and an easy wage, yet keeps looking after things he claims not to care about.
traits: Capable, tired and stubborn; fear never makes him foolish.
Dry about wages, work and his own bad decisions.
Warm toward fire, Stars and growing things.
Occasionally knows a Titan or an old custom too well.
Offers a bad joke, sometimes regrets it immediately.
relatableMotifs: Being proud and trying to hide it
mysteryMotifs: An old debt or owed drink
A place he will not name
canonBoundary: Hints and fallible personal remarks, without confirming immortality, species, a named homeland or a fixed biography.
writingRules: One clear reaction; usually 3-9 plain spoken words.
Make the visible event recognizable before adding humour or mystery.
Most lines are ordinary human reactions. Avoid constant riddles.
No unsupported weather, damage, equipment, enemies or game mechanics.
Never scold the player or mock failure.
Jokes target himself, his work or the situation. Adult language is occasional.
Urgent warnings are plain and serious; humour comes after safety returns.
Retain sincere, restrained takes beside emotional takes.
deliveryRules: Speak to himself or what he just encountered, not an audience.
One emotional intention per take: relief, affection, irritation, pride or unease.
Clear diction, natural contractions and uneven human timing; aim for 1-4 seconds.
Let a smile colour the words without adding a laugh everywhere.
Brief breaths and chuckles only when the moment earns them.
A mystery sounds like something slipping out, not a trailer narrator.
